text: EigenLayer slashing is opt-in and isolated by design. AVSs group operators into Operator Sets, each with its own slashing conditions. text: Withdraw is limited to lamports above the account's still-staked amount plus its rent reserve. If the stake has not been deactivated, the staked amount is the full delegation, so nothing delegated can be withdrawn during warmup. Once the current epoch is at or after deactivation_epoch, the staked amount is the remaining effective stake, so lamports that already cooled can be withdrawn in part during a multi-epoch cooldown. Withdrawing the entire balance (closing the account) needs a staked amount of zero. The withdraw authority must sign. A lockup in force blocks withdrawal unless the lockup custodian signs, but it does not block delegating, deactivating or splitting. (high confidence)

text: Stake changes happen only at epoch boundaries. A stake account delegates to one vote account. When it is delegated in epoch N, the stake program records activation_epoch = N, and during N the whole amount is 'activating' with nothing effective. When it is deactivated in epoch D, the program records deactivation_epoch = D. The effective, activating and deactivating amounts for any epoch are computed from those two numbers plus the cluster stake history. The four states are inactive, activating, active (effective) and deactivating. (high confidence)

text: Kamino now prices all its LSTs at the stake rate read on chain (SOL staked / LST minted), not at the DEX price, so a DEX depeg does not trigger liquidations. Kamino argues a market-price oracle would turn every brief depeg into a cascade, because liquidations add selling, which deepens the depeg, which causes more liquidations; it singles out leveraged Multiply loops. The cost: stake-rate pricing does not cover a fundamental depeg, and it assumes arbitrage restores the market price. If unstaking is blocked and a depeg persists, the protocol could hold collateral worth more on paper than the market pays, and bad debt is socialised among lenders. Kamino lists supply caps, an asset-risk review of each LST's smart contract risk, and monitoring of stake pool health and unstaking delays as mitigations. text: SAM bond rules: a funded Protected Staking Rewards (PSR) bond is required, and settlement charges it each epoch for the previous epoch's stake. Target coverage is 13 epochs. If the bond covers fewer than 5 epochs of expected revenue, the Bond Risk Reduction Mechanism undelegates enough stake that the remaining bond covers the remaining stake for 13 epochs, and charges a fee proportional to the undelegated amount from the bond. A Bid Reduction Penalty applies if a validator's bid falls below its effective bid of the previous 3 epochs. An Activating Stake Fee charges validators for newly activating stake, scaled by how far the bid is above the clearing rate. MIP-19 proposed the risk-reduction mechanism and the activation payment. text: Per-account allowance per epoch is proportional: change = (account_portion / cluster_portion) * (cluster_effective * rate). Activation uses the previous epoch's activating and effective stake; deactivation uses deactivating and effective. The result is capped at the account's own waiting amount. Integer math saturates on overflow ('fail-safe, not fail-open'). Chorus One independently describes the same dependence on new stake relative to stake already active. (medium confidence)

text: Jito (Re)staking is two onchain programs: the Restaking Program (RestkWeAVL8fRGgzhfeoqFhsqKRchg6aa1XrcH96z4Q), a registry of NCNs (node consensus networks) and operators, and the Vault Program (Vau1t6sLNxnzB7ZDsef8TLbPLfyZMYXH8WTNqUdm9g8), which holds deposited SPL tokens, delegates them to approved operators and mints vault receipt tokens (VRTs). Only coordination (delegation, votes, rewards, penalties) is tracked onchain; the NCN's real work runs offchain. The repo describes it as a framework for staking, restaking and liquid restaking on Solana and SVM environments. (high confidence)
